step2.title: Complete the Road
step2.description: The road is still under construction. It takes time to actually begin and complete. Let's advance time and wait for it. Press the "Start" button on the toolbar to progress time. Construction incurs monthly costs while underway.

step3.title: Create a Parcel
step3.description: The road is complete! Now let's create a parcel to build on. Select the parcel icon from the toolbar and use "Create Along Road". When you see red outlines along the road, press confirm to create the parcels.

step4.title: Build a Building
step4.description: Now you can build! Select the building icon from the toolbar and choose "Apartment" from the "Residential" category. You can select any of the parcels you just created as the construction site.

step5.title: Complete the Building
step5.description: Like roads, buildings don't complete instantly. It's still under construction, so advance time and wait for it to finish.

scenario2.title: Set Up Districts
scenario2.description: Learn how to divide your city into districts and set building regulations for each one.

step1.title: Create a District
step1.description: A district is a unit that divides the city into areas, and it is assigned to roads. Press the district button on the icon panel to enter district edit mode: you'll see that the H-shaped road network forms a single district. With the Create tool (the default), click the road with the yellow marker to turn that road and the parcels facing it into a new district.

step2.title: District Created
step2.description: You've split off part of the city as a new district. Districts let you aggregate figures such as prices and population per district, and apply building regulations to the district as a whole. Press the district button again to leave district edit mode.

step3.title: Show Natural Resources
step3.description: Let's check whether this district contains natural resources. Open the display modes with the eye icon in the cockpit at the bottom center of the screen, and turn natural resources on in the natural resources tab. Once they appear, click the ore vein at the yellow marker to open its details.

step4.title: Open District Details
step4.description: You can see there's an ore vein where you created the new district. This area looks like a good spot for a mine. Click the label of the district you just created to open its detail panel.

step5.title: Set Building Regulations
step5.description: Using the building regulations near the bottom of the panel, you can choose which buildings may be built on the parcels in this district. We only want mines here, so click every building other than "Mine" to disable them.

step6.title: Check a Parcel
step6.description: You've set building regulations for the district. Let's confirm they are reflected on the parcels inside it. Click the parcel with the yellow marker to open its detail panel.

step7.title: Regulation Applied
step7.description: Looking near the bottom of the parcel panel, you can see the district's regulation allowing only "Mine" is reflected here. You can no longer build anything other than a mine on this parcel.

scenario3.title: Build the Infrastructure
scenario3.description: Learn how to deliver electricity to your city by building power plants, substations, and power lines.

step1.description: The apartment building in this town doesn't have electricity yet. Click the apartment building with the yellow marker to open its details, pick one of the tenants in the "Building Info" tab, then open its "Trade" tab: you can see that the Acquired amount of Electricity is 0.
step1.title: Check the Apartment Building

step2.description: To generate electricity, you need a power plant. Build a "Solar Power Plant" on the parcel with the yellow marker on the flat land west of town. It would normally take time to complete, but since this is a tutorial, the construction period is skipped once confirmed and the plant is completed.
step2.title: Build a Solar Power Plant

step3.description: The high-voltage electricity produced by a power plant can't be used by households as it is. Build a "Substation" on the parcel with the yellow marker next to the apartment building to convert it into power that homes can use. A substation's electricity reaches a certain area around it.
step3.title: Build a Substation

step4.description: Open "Infrastructure" on the icon panel and choose "Power Line" under "Electricity". Draw a line from the solar power plant's connection terminal to the connection terminal of the substation in town. Even though they're far apart, you can draw it as a single line by linking the terminals in a straight line. Once confirmed, the power line is completed and the connection is checked.
step4.title: Connect with a Power Line

step5.description: Advance epochs and check whether the substation is receiving high-voltage electricity. Click the substation to open its details and, in the "Trade" tab, make sure the Received amount of High-voltage electricity isn't 0. It takes a few epochs for the power plant to start up and the power to arrive.
step5.title: Confirm the Power Supply

step6.description: Finally, open a tenant's "Trade" tab from the apartment building's details as in step 1, and check that the Acquired amount of Electricity is no longer 0. It may take a few more epochs for power to reach households. Generation, transmission and transformation linked together bring power to homes — that's how power infrastructure works, and water supply works the same way.
step6.title: Infrastructure Complete

scenario4.title: Build a Railway
scenario4.description: Learn how to open a rail line by building tracks, a depot, power lines, a platform, and a station house in order.

step2.title: Lay the Track
step2.description: First, the track the trains will run on. Open 'Track Construction' from the icon panel on the left and pick 'Electrified Surface Track' on the 'Track' tab. A single track only runs one way, so you need a double track for round trips. Set the parallel track count to 2, then lay it straight east–west on the open land north of the road. Left-click to add a vertex and right-click to confirm.

step3.title: Build the Depot
step3.description: Track without rolling stock still won't move anyone. Vehicles are supplied to a line from a depot. Open 'Construction' from the icon panel, choose 'Rail Depot', and build it on the empty parcel prepared along the road. Construction would normally take time, but this is a tutorial, so it finishes as soon as you press the completion button.

step4.title: Connect a Siding
step4.description: A depot that isn't connected to the track can't send out any vehicles. The depot has a 'connection terminal' node. Open 'Track Construction' again, pick 'Electrified Surface Track' (a single track is fine here), and lay a siding from that terminal to the main line. Snap one end to the depot terminal and the other to the main track.

step5.title: Connect the Power Line
step5.description: An electrified track only moves trains once current flows through its overhead wires. Open 'Road' from the icon panel, choose 'Power Line' under 'Electricity' on the 'Infrastructure' tab, and connect the solar power plant's terminal to the depot's terminal. The depot terminal accepts both track and power connections, so once power reaches it, it flows through the siding to the whole track network.

step6.title: Build the Platform
step6.description: Next comes the platform where passengers wait. On the 'Platform' tab of 'Track Construction', choose 'Electrified Surface Rail Platform' and lay a short section along the main line. A platform is a kind of track too, so the trick is to lay it so it joins the main line smoothly. Use the platform side setting to choose which side of the track the platform sits on.

step7.title: Build the Station House
step7.description: A platform on its own doesn't belong to any station yet. On the 'Station House' tab of 'Track Construction', choose 'Simple Overbridge Station House' and draw its line so that it crosses the platform you just built. Every platform crossed by that line is gathered into one station, and station buildings are placed at both ends of the line.

step8.title: Open the Line
step8.description: Finally, create the line the trains will run on. Open 'Public Transport' from the icon panel and press '+ New Line'. Choose 'Medium-Distance Rail Line' as the type, then click on the platform in the 3D view to place stops. Set the fare and the target headway, and press 'Create' to open the line.

step9.title: The Railway Opens
step9.description: Well done. Track to run on, a depot to supply vehicles, power lines to feed the wires, a platform and station house to form a station, and a line running over it all — a railway is built from all of these pieces together. Advance time and the trains will start running and earning fares. Stations make the area around them convenient, so try attracting housing and commerce nearby.

complete.title: Tutorial Complete
complete.description: Congratulations! You have completed the tutorial. Press "Finish" to close the guide and keep playing this city freely.

tutorial.failed: Condition not met. Please try again.

guide.openRoad: Open the construction panel using the road icon.
guide.selectRoad: Select the ground-level two-lane street. Only the required variant is available.
guide.placeStart: Left-click inside the cyan circle to place the start of the road.
guide.placeEnd: Left-click inside the yellow circle to place the end of the road.
guide.finalizeRoad: Right-click in the 3D view to finish the road shape.
guide.confirmRoad: Confirm in the construction panel to save the road, then press Complete.
guide.failed: Setup or communication failed. Retry; if the problem persists, exit and start the tutorial in a new city.
guide.placementRequired: Use the road variant and positions shown by the guide.
guide.finishFailed: Could not finish the tutorial. Please try again.

trade.title: Start international trade
trade.description: Learn how to export goods by sea and import them by rail by building a container port and an international freight station.

step1.description: Build a "Container Terminal" on the coastal parcel with the yellow marker. Once confirmed, the construction period is skipped.
step1.title: Build a container port

step2.description: Advance epochs and check the food exports in the port's details. It takes a few epochs for the factory's production and transport to get going.
step2.title: Confirm food exports

step3.description: Build an "International Freight Station" on the parcel with the yellow marker along the road. At the eastern border, there is a railway leading into the neighboring country and a border freight station.
step3.title: Build an international freight station

step4.open: Open "Track Construction" on the icon panel and choose "Container Freight Platform" on the "Platform" tab.
step4.place: Lay a platform north of the international freight station, parallel to it. Switch "Platform Side" so that the platform is on the station building's side (the south side) before confirming. If you lay it from west to east, choose "Inside". When you're done, press the "Completed" button.
step4.title: Build a platform beside the station

step5.description: Using "Railway Track" on the "Track" tab, lay track from the east end of the platform to the west end of the border freight station's platform. Once confirmed, the track is completed and the connection is checked.
step5.title: Lay track to the border

step6.build: Build a "Rail Depot" on the parcel with the yellow marker along the road.
step6.branch: Lay a siding from the connection terminal on the north side of the depot to the main line. Join the main line at a shallow angle heading east rather than at a right angle. When you're done, press the "Completed" button.
step6.title: Build a depot and connect it to the main line

step7.description: Open "Infrastructure" on the icon panel and use "Power Line" under "Electricity" to connect the connection terminal of the solar power plant east of town to the depot's connection terminal.
step7.title: Supply power to the depot

step8.description: In "Public Transport", press "+ New line" and choose "International Freight Line" as the line type. Place stops on the platforms of the international freight station and the border freight station, and open the line. Once confirmed, the city's import gateway switches from the port to the international freight station.
step8.title: Open the international freight line

step9.description: Advance epochs and check the imports in the international freight station's details. Procuring vehicles and getting transport up and running takes a few epochs.
step9.title: Confirm rail imports

highway.title: Build a motorway
highway.description: Learn how to build an elevated motorway and ramps to create an interchange connecting to local streets.

step1.title: Cross above the street
step1.description: Build a motorway across the central street at least 6 m above ground. A north–south route at 10 m works. Confirmation completes it.

step2.title: Name the motorway
step2.description: Register the new motorway as a named road and enter its name in the details panel.

step3.title: Build a ramp
step3.description: Connect the elevated motorway to the central street with a ramp. Confirmation completes construction and checks for an interchange.

step4.title: Inspect the interchange
step4.description: Open the interchange details and confirm the connection between the street and motorway.

mining.title: Mine resources
mining.description: Learn how to mine ore, transport it by rail, and export it by building a mine, freight stations, and a bulk port.

step1.description: Turn on the natural resources display with the eye icon in the cockpit at the bottom of the screen, then click the ore vein on the western slope of the central mountain (yellow marker) to open its details.
step1.title: Inspect the ore vein

step2.description: Build a "Mine" on the parcel with the yellow marker above the ore vein. Select "Mine" in the construction panel and click the parcel to place it. Once confirmed, the construction period is skipped because this is a tutorial, and the mine is completed.
step2.title: Build a mine

step3.description: Build an "Ore Loading Station" on the parcel with the yellow marker at the foot of the mountain, on the north side of the main street. Ore dug at the mine is gathered here by truck and loaded onto freight trains.
step3.title: Build a loading station at the foot of the mountain

step4.description: Build an "Ore Unloading Station" on the parcel with the yellow marker at the corner of the harbor road. Ore brought in by rail is unloaded here. Be careful not to mix it up with the similarly named "Oil Unloading Station".
step4.title: Build an unloading station near the port

step5.description: Build a "Bulk Port" on the seafront parcel with the yellow marker at the end of the harbor road. The ore is exported overseas from here.
step5.title: Build a bulk port

step6.open: Open "Track Construction" on the icon panel and choose "Ore Freight Platform" on the "Platform" tab.
step6.loading: Lay a platform north of the loading station, parallel to it. Switching "Platform Side" changes where the platform appears in the preview, so make sure the platform is on the station building's side (the south side) before confirming. If you lay it from west to east, choose "Inside". The site slopes steeply downhill. If you get a grade error, adjust the "Embankment Height" to keep the platform level.
step6.unloading: Lay a platform north of the unloading station in the same way, so that the platform is on the station building's side. When you're done, press the "Completed" button.
step6.title: Build platforms beside the stations

step7.description: Using "Railway Track" on the "Track" tab, lay track from the east end of the unloading station's platform to the west end of the loading station's platform (a single track is fine). Once confirmed, the track and platforms are completed and the connection is checked.
step7.title: Connect the two stations by rail

step8.build: Trains are dispatched from a depot. Build a "Rail Depot" on the parcel with the yellow marker along the main street.
step8.branch: Lay a siding from the connection terminal on the north side of the depot to the main line. The trick is to join the main line at a shallow angle heading east rather than at a right angle (real turnouts can't turn at large angles). When you're done, press the "Completed" button.
step8.title: Build a depot and connect it to the main line

step9.description: The track is electrified, and power flows into it from the depot's connection terminal. Open "Infrastructure" on the icon panel and use "Power Line" under "Electricity" to connect the connection terminal of the town's solar power plant to the depot's connection terminal.
step9.title: Supply power to the depot

step10.description: In "Public Transport" on the icon panel, press "+ New line" and choose "Ore Freight Line" as the line type. Click on the platforms at the loading and unloading stations to place stops, then press "Create" to open the line.
step10.title: Open the ore freight line

step11.description: Run epochs to get mining, loading, rail transport, unloading, and exports going. Procuring vehicles and getting transport up and running takes a few epochs.
step11.title: Advance epochs

step12.description: Check the ore exports in the bulk port's details. If nothing has been exported yet, advance more epochs.
step12.title: Confirm ore exports

tourism.title: Develop tourism
tourism.description: Learn how to attract tourists and encourage visits to restaurants and use of bus services by building a hotel and a passenger terminal.

step1.description: Build a "Tourist Hotel" on the parcel with the yellow marker east of the ancient ruins by the sea. Once confirmed, the construction period is skipped.
step1.title: Build a hotel by the ruins

step2.description: Build a "Cruise Terminal" on the marked parcel at the port. A bus route and a bus depot are already in place between the port and the ruins.
step2.title: Build a cruise terminal

step3.description: Advance epochs to welcome tourists. It takes a few epochs for operations to get going.
step3.title: Advance epochs

step4.description: Check the sales of the restaurant in front of the ruins and the ridership of the bus route. You succeed once both have risen above their starting values and tourists have arrived.
step4.title: Check for higher sales and bus ridership

intro.basic: Welcome! You are the mayor of this city. In this tutorial, you'll learn the basic flow of city building: laying a road, waiting for it to be completed, and putting up a building on land parcels.
intro.scenario2: You can manage a city by dividing it into "districts". In this tutorial, you'll learn how to create a new district by selecting roads, check where natural resources are found, and regulate which buildings can be built in each district.
intro.scenario3: The setting is a harbor town in the northwest of an island surrounded by coral shallows. The town has no electricity yet. You'll build a solar power plant on the flat land to the west, away from town, deliver power to the town's substation through a power line, and learn how power infrastructure is made up of three stages: generation, transmission, and transformation.
intro.scenario4: Laying track alone won't get trains running. In this tutorial, you'll set up the track, a depot, power lines, a platform, and a station building in order, then finally open a line, learning how a railway runs on a combination of many elements.
intro.trade: This city is connected by rail to a neighboring country at its eastern border and faces the sea to the west. In this tutorial, you'll create two trade routes: exporting a factory's food by sea through a container port, and importing goods by rail over a freight line you lay to the border.
intro.highway: As a city grows, local streets alone can no longer handle all the cars. In this tutorial, you'll learn how to build an elevated motorway that crosses over a local street, then connect the two with ramps to create an interchange.
intro.mining: The setting is an island surrounded by coral shallows. An ore vein lies untouched in the central mountain. In this tutorial, you'll learn the whole flow — mining ore in the mountain, carrying it by freight rail from a loading station at the foot of the mountain to the harbor town, and exporting it overseas from a bulk port — while building the track and depot yourself.
intro.tourism: The harbor town on this island, surrounded by coral seas, has ancient ruins by the shore. In this tutorial, you'll attract tourists by building a hotel beside the ruins and a cruise terminal at the port, and see the town's restaurants and bus route come alive.
intro.heading: In this tutorial

tip1.title: The Epoch System
tip1.description: In this game, you can take your time to plan budgets and construction before advancing time. The city's state won't change until you click 'Run Simulation'.

tip2.title: Maintaining Public Facilities
tip2.description: Public facilities like fire and police stations degrade over time. Lacking maintenance budget reduces their efficiency, or in the worst case, causes them to collapse.

tip3.title: Road Connections & Parcels
tip3.description: Parcels belong to districts based on the road they face. Buildings cannot be constructed on unconnected parcels, preventing any economic activity.

tip4.title: Citizen Needs & QOL
tip4.description: Citizens live by consuming products like food, healthcare, and entertainment. When these are supplied sufficiently, their Quality of Life (QOL) improves.

tip5.title: Approximate Simulation
tip5.description: To keep the game running smoothly even as cities grow huge, traffic and supply/demand are calculated using approximate mathematical models instead of simulating every single car and citizen individually.

tip6.title: Build Fire Stations in the City
tip6.description: Fire stations should be near where buildings are dense. A station on the outskirts won't make it in time when it counts.

tip7.title: Slow Down on Curves
tip7.description: Set lower speed limits on roads with sharp curves. Roads that are too fast see a lot more accidents.

tip8.title: Schools Make Cities Prosper
tip8.description: Educating citizens opens the door to more advanced industries. If you want hospitals and factories, start by investing in schools.

tip9.title: Don't Forget Maintenance
tip9.description: Buildings deteriorate and can collapse if left alone. Open the budget panel and make sure your maintenance allocation isn't sitting at zero.

tip10.title: Fire Spreads
tip10.description: Fires can spread to neighboring buildings in dense areas. Spread your fire stations across different parts of the city rather than clustering them.

tip11.title: Spread Police Stations Too
tip11.description: Like fire stations, police stations lose effectiveness with distance. Build them near areas where crime is rising.

tip12.title: Use Immigration Filters
tip12.description: You can set immigration requirements in the Regulation window. Filtering by skill or age lets you attract the kind of residents your city needs.

tip13.title: Districts Help You Stay Organized
tip13.description: Grouping roads into districts lets you view stats and set regulations by area. Once your city starts growing, districts become essential.

tip14.title: Better Safe Than Sorry
tip14.description: If critical infrastructure shuts down due to accidents or disasters, the city's economy will take a massive hit. Build redundant facilities to keep backups ready.

tip15.title: Don't Let It Sprawl
tip15.description: When there are not enough parcels for the demand, roads and parcels appear on their own in a disorderly way. Develop the city deliberately to keep slums from forming.

tip16.title: Industrial Clusters
tip16.description: Productivity rises when similar industries or raw material producers are nearby. Create industrial zones and tech districts to bring businesses together.

tip17.title: Can You Work Around the Clock?
tip17.description: Longer working hours raise productivity. Entertainment spending and health take the hit.

tip18.title: Commuter Hell
tip18.description: Longer commutes mean less spending on entertainment.

tip19.title: Think Ahead
tip19.description: You cannot run trains longer than station platforms. Build your railway with room to grow.

tip20.title: Bury the Problem
tip20.description: Underground roads produce neither noise nor air pollution. Some problems really can be solved by burying them.

tip21.title: In the Shadow of Progress
tip21.description: Tall buildings cast shadows on their neighbors, making the area less pleasant to live in. Your city may have a bright future, but its streets could be in the dark.

tip22.title: Trade the Keys for a Transit Pass
tip22.description: With convenient public transit, even wealthy residents can give up their cars and spend their money on other things.

tip23.title: Now Transporting: Air
tip23.description: Even empty buses take up road space. Do not turn your congestion relief plan into a traffic jam.

tip24.title: Moles Pay No Rent
tip24.description: Tunnels below a certain depth need no land acquisition. If negotiations get tough, dig deeper.

tip25.title: The High Road to Work
tip25.description: Cable cars provide transport even on steep terrain. If public transit is hard to build, leave your citizens hanging.

tip26.title: An Electrical Traffic Jam
tip26.description: Spare generating capacity is no help if the power lines cannot carry it. Before building another power plant, check for bottlenecks along the way.

tip27.title: An Unfortunate Accident
tip27.description: A building that stands in the way of development can be blown up and passed off as an accident. Public sentiment takes a heavy hit, so buy it and demolish it properly when you can.

tip28.title: No Land? Take to the Sea
tip28.description: Running out of room on land? Build offshore oil platforms and wind turbines out at sea. Connect them to your onshore transport grid with undersea pipelines and power cables.

tip29.title: Red Light Hell
tip29.description: Every intersection adds another red light. Grid layouts packed too closely together will trap drivers at every single block, and their patience will run out long before they reach their destination.

tip30.title: Good Line of Sight
tip30.description: Radio towers cover a wider area the higher they are built and the higher the ground. Signals blocked by mountains can't be overcome by sheer willpower alone.

tip31.title: Bounty of the Sea
tip31.description: If you can't find a freshwater source, you can build a desalination plant along the coast. It does require significant power, though. Finding water leads right into finding electricity.

tip32.title: Another Form of Policing
tip32.description: Unemployment is one of the root causes of crime. Don't just build police stations—provide jobs. Before agonizing over your police budget, consider investing in employment programs.

tip33.title: Bills for the Future
tip33.description: Both buildings and roads demand ongoing maintenance once built. If you overbuild just because you have spare cash, repair bills will haunt you later. Remember, that future mayor is still you.

tip34.title: Don't Over-Pump
tip34.description: If you pump water faster than the aquifer can replenish, you'll eventually face a shortage. Adding more pumps won't create more water.

hint.buildingConstruction: Select a parcel to plan a building. It takes some time from planning to completion.
hint.parcelCreation: Hold Ctrl to pick a creation method from the radial menu, then click a target in the 3D view. Adjust the size in the panel and confirm.
hint.transitCreation: Left-click to place stops in order; click the first stop to close the loop. Drag a segment to add a waypoint, drag a point to move it, right-click to delete. For a round trip, also place the return stops.
hint.transitManagement: List of public transit lines. Adjust fares and headways, or create and delete lines. Fares affect residents' route choice. Fares that are too high reduce ridership and increase car ownership.
hint.pathConstruction: Construct roads and railways. Click on the terrain in the 3D view: left-click to add vertices, right-click to confirm the shape, and drag vertices to reposition them. Hold Ctrl to open the settings menu (curve/straight and snapping). Use 3/4 keys to change embankment/cut height.
hint.pathConstructionElevated: Construct roads and railways. Click on the terrain in the 3D view: left-click to add vertices, right-click to confirm the shape, and drag vertices to reposition them. Hold Ctrl to open the settings menu (curve/straight and snapping). Use PageUp/PageDown or 1/2 to change height, and 3/4 keys to change embankment/cut height.
hint.districtEdit: Create, expand and merge "districts", the units for regulations and statistics. Hold Ctrl in the 3D view to switch tools. Create tool: left-click a road to create a new district in the shown color (a new color is drawn each time you pick the tool). Expand tool: right-click to pick the district to grow, then left-click roads to pull them into it. Merge tool: right-click to pick the district to merge into, then left-click another district to open the confirmation panel. The selected district's color and name are shown next to the mouse cursor. Press the button again to exit.
hint.bulldozer: Bulldozer mode. Left-click to remove empty parcels, planned buildings, planned roads, and terrain props (scattered props are removed as a whole area after confirmation). Press the button again to exit.
hint.cityBudget: Decide how to allocate the funds earned from taxes and business operations for the next period. When the government purchases materials for road construction or public facility operations, it can only do so within the budget decided here. If the budget is insufficient, employees of public facilities may be dismissed. As a general rule, plan to use up all the cash you earn rather than saving it, and give it back to the city.
hint.resourceEdit: Create a natural resource area. Select a resource type, then click on the terrain. Left-click to add a vertex, click an edge to insert a vertex, and right-click to remove a vertex. Drag a vertex to reposition it.
hint.grading: Draw the area to develop. Left-click the terrain to place vertices, then right-click to close the area and see the estimate. After closing, drag a vertex to move it, click an edge to add a vertex, and right-click a vertex to remove it. Land is leveled to the surface of the road it faces; an area reaching into the sea is reclaimed, and its sea-facing edges become quays.
